question: A book is sold at three successive discounts of 8%, 4%, and 5%. If the marked price of the book is ₹3,125, find its net selling price.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net SP = MP × (100 − D₁)% × (100 − D₂)% × (100 − D₃)%

Net SP = 3125 × (92 ÷ 100) × (96 ÷ 100) × (95 ÷ 100)

Net SP = 3125 × (23 ÷ 25) × (24 ÷ 25) × (19 ÷ 20)

Net SP = 5 × 23 × 24 × (19 ÷ 20)

Net SP = 23 × 6 × 19 = 2622

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,622.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) of the book = ₹3,125

Successive discounts = 8%, 4%, and 5%

**Calculations:**

⇒ First discount = 8% of ₹3,125 = (8 ÷ 100) × 3125 = ₹250

⇒ Price after first discount = 3125 − 250 = ₹2,875

⇒ Second discount = 4% of ₹2,875 = (4 ÷ 100) × 2875 = ₹115

⇒ Price after second discount = 2875 − 115 = ₹2,760

⇒ Third discount = 5% of ₹2,760 = (5 ÷ 100) × 2760 = ₹138

⇒ Net Selling Price = 2760 − 138 = ₹2,622

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,622.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Discount of Two Successive Discounts

When two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is calculated as: D = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Marked Price vs Selling Price

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP) of an article. If D% is the discount, the Selling Price (SP) is obtained as: SP = MP × (100 − D) ÷ 100.

Commutative Property of Successive Discounts

The order in which successive discounts are applied does not affect the final selling price. For example, applying 8%, then 4%, yields the exact same net selling price as applying 4%, then 8%.
